title: Players who couldn't name keys; changing key in a tune
summary: Arnold Jr. describes old players with good ears who could not name keys, an old pianist, and bands repeating a tune in new keys.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You see, and then, too, there were bands, I've seen guys play like that. There were bands where the guy knew so little about music. I think this is kind of the part, you know, that I bring this out. Of course, I found this out when I was a kid. He knew so little about music until he couldn't tell you he was playing in the G. Well, if I played a tune and I said, well, man, Tiger Ray, B flat, well, he couldn't do that. And he'd blow that piece on the horn to establish the key. And everybody would listen real close. And then he'd know what key was in it. You see? Well, how I first found it out, I was playing on a job with an old fella. And somebody, well, you know, we was playing some old tunes. When the dance is really swinging or the party or whatever they're playing, and they get, they had a part of their howl, and the band, not really howl, but the guy is running and saying, all right, everybody for themselves. And then the guys be playing, they're going to be, and he said, band out. You know, well, that's when they're going to swing and really strike that groove, you know. And he's swinging. And then the band is swinging. So after the band finishes the tune, and the people clapping, they look like, you know, they're crazy about the tune, and the guy is doing it again. He's going to go. And I have seen bands that did that three times, and every time they pick it up in a different key. Because the guy doesn't know his horn. But he can play it. Man, he can play you anything. But what happened, he didn't know his horn. And when he would pick that same tune over again, he did it in another key. And everybody followed him. And I mean, if you know the thing about music, man, that's kind of amazing. Yeah, it is. You know? He knew something if he could do that. Well, he had terrific ears, and that's what most all the guys back there had. They could hear everything.
